mbm-1176.quote: I cut a paper crane with a row of tiny waves inside its wings. On my red wall the bird looks sleepy. Hold it against the sky and the little waves start moving whenever a cloud goes by.

mbm-1177.clue: I keep a watch face with no watch.
mbm-1177.quote: I found an old watch dial beside a bench at the golf course. The groundskeeper set it into a wooden ball marker for me. It is always ten past tee time as far as I’m concerned.

mbm-1178.clue: I know the chord that opens a window.
mbm-1178.quote: When I practice cuatro my neighbor leaves her kitchen window shut until I get the opening right. Then up goes the sash and out comes her harmony. I can hear the latch click before the first word.

mbm-1179.clue: I found the map on the wrapping paper.
mbm-1179.quote: A market seller wrapped my little brass compass in an old street map. The shop itself was marked with a blue cross. I put the map under the compass in a frame and can always find my way back.

mbm-1180.clue: I made a moon with a thumbhole.
mbm-1180.quote: I wanted a clay lamp that threw a crescent onto my wall. I pinched the opening around my thumb. When I light it, I can see the bump where my thumbnail pressed the moon.

mbm-1181.clue: I cut the second butterfly very slowly.
mbm-1181.quote: I was making papel picado for our courtyard when two butterflies came loose at the wing. I joined their antennae with a fine paper strip. In the breeze they bob together like partners at a dance.

mbm-1182.clue: I sleeve the ugliest card first.
mbm-1182.quote: My favorite fantasy creature is a grumpy brown turnip with one tooth. I built a whole deck around getting him to the feast. Other players bring dragons. I bring a restaurant reservation.

mbm-1183.clue: I draw the doorway before the flowers.
mbm-1183.quote: I cut a papel picado street with little opening doors beneath a row of marigolds. My brother holds the paper up to the light while I cut. He always wants to know who lives in the last house.

mbm-1184.clue: My jump log smells like grass.
mbm-1184.quote: I landed in a freshly cut field on a clear Sunday. My instructor suggested I press a blade of grass into my logbook beside the drawing of my canopy. It’s the one page that still smells like the landing.

mbm-1185.clue: I always read the page with the ink blot twice.
mbm-1185.quote: An old copy of my favorite novel has a blue blot across a word. Each time through I choose a new word to put underneath. Last summer’s word changed the whole argument between the sisters.

mbm-1186.clue: I can judge a roll by the dust.
mbm-1186.quote: At our bocce court one corner stays powdery under the trees. I rolled through it so slowly the ball picked up a pale belt of dust. My uncle called it Saturn and refused to wipe it.

mbm-1187.clue: I make room for two pencil stubs.
mbm-1187.quote: I stitched a small leather case for the colored pencils in my travel sketchbook. My daughter went looking for a spare pocket, so I added one in yellow with enough room for both our favorite colors.

mbm-1188.clue: I can hem a curtain without taking down the whole sky.
mbm-1188.quote: I shortened my mother’s flowered kitchen curtains while she held up the spare cloth. One tiny star ended up inside the hem. We decided it was sleeping until somebody needed a wish.

mbm-1189.clue: I sit where the apricots sit.
mbm-1189.quote: The fruit seller puts a chair in the patch of afternoon sun beside the apricot crates. I sit there on my lunch break and lend the seller my straw hat when the glare makes the scales hard to read.

mbm-1190.clue: I found the bird by watching the ants.
mbm-1190.quote: I saw a trail of ants moving away from a dead branch. A woodpecker was drilling at the other end, invisible behind the trunk. I walked two paces sideways and finally saw the red crest.

mbm-1191.clue: I put a moon on the disc myself.
mbm-1191.quote: I painted a silver crescent on our plain flying disc so my friends could tell when it was spinning cleanly. At dusk the crescent makes one bright circle. Our last round always runs late.

mbm-1192.clue: I drew the pattern on a cereal carton.
mbm-1192.quote: I cut quilt diamonds from the side of the breakfast box. One still had a cartoon eye printed on it. My brother kept it as a stencil and put a face on every scrap I left behind.

mbm-1193.clue: I gave the sugar bowl a stairway.
mbm-1193.quote: I pinched three tiny steps into the side of a clay bowl before firing it. My nephew says that’s how the spoon gets up. I always leave the spoon at the bottom step for him to discover.

mbm-1194.clue: I quilt with the curtains open.
mbm-1194.quote: Light shines through a scrap differently from the way it looks on the table. I held one dull gray square to the window and found tiny blue flowers. They got the center of my new quilt.

mbm-1195.clue: I’m the thunder behind the curtain.
mbm-1195.quote: At our community theater I shake a thin metal sheet for storms. Once the lead forgot to close her umbrella and I had to hold the thunder for a full minute. We both took the weather very seriously.

mbm-1196.clue: I catch the reflection before the boat.
mbm-1196.quote: When I paint at the river I start with the colored streaks on the water. Boats tend to leave halfway through my pictures. At least the paint remembers which one had the little red cabin.

mbm-1197.clue: My lucky bocce ball has a little scratch.
mbm-1197.quote: I carved an arrow into the wooden stand for my set so the scratch faces up. My sister says it points toward the target. I tell her that depends entirely on who is rolling.

mbm-1198.clue: I made a quilt for the kitchen wall.
mbm-1198.quote: It shows four jars, each pieced from fabric the color of whatever we pick in summer. My aunt embroidered little flies above the yellow plum jar. They are the only flies Mum lets stay.

mbm-1199.clue: I keep a lift ticket in my wool hat.
mbm-1199.quote: I tucked the ticket from my first run with my dad into the folded brim. Last winter he came down the same slope behind me. At the bottom I handed him the hat and waited for him to find it.

mbm-1200.clue: I count the lookout by the wind.
mbm-1200.quote: I tied a little strip of cloth to my walking stick. It hung still in the valley and snapped straight out when I reached the ridge. I knew I had made the top before I saw the view.
